items.prompt: Black to move after 4.Nc3. Count Black's guards of d5 and White's attackers. How many more guards than attackers does Black have?

claims.statement: Three black units attack d5.
Two white units attack d5.

hints: Count the black guards: pawn first, then knight, then queen.
White's attackers on d5: the c4 pawn and the c3 knight.
Three guards minus two attackers.
items.explain: Black guards d5 three times (the c6 pawn, the f6 knight and the queen) against White's two attackers (the c4 pawn and the c3 knight), one more. So d5 is safe and Black is free to choose when to take on c4: taking wins a pawn, which Black can keep with ...b5 or give back for development.

items.prompt: Black played ...e6 instead of ...Bf5. To how many squares can the c8 bishop move now?

claims.statement: The c8 bishop can reach exactly one square.
The pawn stands on e6.

hints: Look at the diagonal from c8 towards h3.
Which pawn now stands on that diagonal?
Only the square next to the bishop, d7, is free.
items.explain: The pawn on e6 shuts the c8 bishop behind its own pawns for now: d7 is its only square. Black can still play ...e6 first (masters did in 347 games, with close to equal results) but must then free the bishop another way, so bishop first is the simpler plan.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has taken on c4 and can defend the pawn with ...b5. Find a good move (several work; a4 and e4 are the most common).

claims.statement: After a4 a white pawn attacks b5.
At depth 16 a4, e4, Ne5 and g3 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.
At depth 16 e3 is at least 0.15 pawn worse than the best move.

hints: What can Black do to keep the extra pawn?
Which white pawn can fight the b5 square, and which can fight for the centre?
One pawn is on the a-file, one on the e-file.
items.explain: a4 takes control of b5, so ...b5 can be met by axb5. e4 builds the centre at once. Ne5 and g3 are also sound at depth 16; all four are about equal, within 0.4 pawn of the best.

feedback_by_move.e2e3: e3 lets Black keep the pawn with ...b5; the position after ...b5 and a4, b4 is about level, so e3 gives up the small edge a4 keeps.

items.prompt: Black to move after 5.e4. White has left out a4. Find the move that holds the extra pawn.

claims.statement: At depth 16 ...b5 is the engine's first choice.
At depth 16 ...Bg4 is at least 0.5 pawn worse than ...b5.

hints: Which Black pawn can protect the pawn on c4?
What did a4 stop in the main line?
The b-pawn advances two squares.
items.explain: Without a4 the pawn on b5 would be safe, so ...b5 is the move: it protects c4 with a pawn. At depth 16 the other move tested, ...Bg4, is at least 0.5 pawn worse. Masters reached this position in 185 games and played ...b5 in 179 of them (77 White wins, 52 draws, 50 Black wins).

feedback_by_move.c8g4: Bg4 develops the bishop but leaves the c4 pawn without a pawn guard. At depth 16 it is at least 0.5 pawn worse than ...b5.

items.prompt: White to move. The knight on c3 is pinned to the king. Find a good move (several work, including castling and Qe2).

claims.statement: The pinned knight on c3 has no legal move.
At depth 16 O-O, Qe2 and Nh4 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.
At depth 16 e4 is at least 1 pawn worse than the best move.

hints: What does the bishop on b4 pin the knight to?
Which move takes the king off the pin line?
Castling ends the pin; the queen move prepares it and defends c4.
items.explain: Castling puts the king on g1, off the diagonal, so the knight is free again. Qe2 defends the bishop on c4 and keeps castling for next move. Nh4 hits the f5 bishop. At depth 16 all three are about equal, within 0.4 pawn of the best.

feedback_by_move.e3e4: e4 hits the bishop, but the pinned knight cannot recapture, so ...Bxe4 wins the pawn. At depth 16 it is at least 1 pawn worse than castling.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a good move (several work; two of them aim at the c4 pawn, by a knight move or by a pawn move that opens a bishop).

claims.statement: After Ne5 the knight attacks c4.
After e3 the bishop on f1 attacks c4.
At depth 16 Ne5, e3 and Nh4 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: What is on c4 now?
Which white piece could attack it in one move?
The knight on f3, or a pawn move that opens the f1 bishop.
items.explain: Ne5 attacks c4 at once. e3 opens the diagonal of the f1 bishop, which then attacks c4. Nh4 hits the bishop first. At depth 16 all three are about equal, within 0.4 pawn of the best.

items.prompt: Black to move after 7.Bxc4. Find a sound developing move (several work).

claims.statement: At depth 16 ...Bb4, ...Nbd7, ...Bg6 and ...h6 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.
At depth 16 ...b5 is at least 1.5 pawns worse than the best move.

hints: Which of your pieces are still at home?
What does the a4 pawn attack?
Develop a piece instead of pushing a pawn.
items.explain: Each of the four keeps the setup intact: three develop a piece and ...h6 gives the bishop a retreat. The pawn push ...b5 runs into axb5: the a-pawn was placed to answer exactly that.

feedback_by_move.b7b5: b5 meets axb5 cxb5 Bxb5+ and White is a pawn up with the better position. At depth 16 it is at least 1.5 pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 Nc3, Nh4, cxd5 and Bd3 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: Which pieces are still at home?
Is any piece of yours attacked or loose?
Develop, or attack the bishop that left the chain.
items.explain: Nc3 develops and supports e4 and d5; Nh4 attacks the bishop; cxd5 and Bd3 are also fine. At depth 16 all four are within 0.4 pawn of the best move.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 Qe2, O-O, Nh4 and Qb3 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: Is any piece of yours still undeveloped or on its first rank?
Your king is still on e1.
Castle, or prepare it with a developing queen move.
items.explain: Qe2 and O-O finish the setup; Nh4 and Qb3 are also sound. At depth 16 all four are within 0.4 pawn of the best.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 ...h6, ...Nbd7, ...Bg6, ...c5 and ...Re8 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: What does your opponent's last move attack?
Which of your pieces is not yet developed or may be hit?
The bishop on f5 can be asked to move; the knight on b8 is still at home.
items.explain: Black has several sound moves here: a pawn move that gives the bishop a retreat, the last knight, the bishop itself, the ...c5 break or a rook to the centre. At depth 16 all five are within 0.4 pawn of the best.
